text:
All tests pass and every case from the issue now behaves correctly. The fix was minimal — two one-line changes in `versions/compare.py`:

1. `parse` now returns `[int(p) for p in parts]` instead of the raw string parts, so release components compare numerically (matching its documented contract). This fixes `1.10.0` vs `1.9.0`, `2.0.0` vs `10.0.0`, and makes `1.02.0` equal to `1.2.0`.
2. `compare`'s `zip_longest` fillvalue changed from `"0"` to `0` to match the new int type, so missing trailing components still count as 0 (`"1.2"` == `"1.2.0"`).

Pre-release comparison logic was untouched and still works as before.
